name: Solenne Auric Datalink Bracelet
description:
Wide-cuff bracelet in 22-carat gold-analog plating over a titanium substrate, inlaid with a continuous band of lab-grown black opal that shifts between deep violet and copper-green depending on ambient light. Embedded along the inner face is a passive data-chip array — twelve chips, each holding encrypted social credentials, financial access keys, or personal records. The clasp is a Japanese-style fold-over in white gold-analog, stamped with Solenne's Spire atelier mark.

Worn as jewelry. Functions as an entire secure wallet, identity suite, and social passport.
functionality: Twelve passive NFC chips store financial credentials, encrypted identity data, and social access keys. BCI-synced release — only the wearer's neural signature unlocks the chip array for write access. Read-only pings are blocked by the titanium substrate except at designated contact points. No power source required.
what_it_says: Everything you need to know about this person is in that bracelet, and you will never be authorized to read it.
story_hooks: A bracelet matching this description appeared in a Tier-1 pawn shop — the chip array was wiped, but the clasp stamp is genuine Solenne, and the atelier has no record of the sale.
The black opal shifts color in proximity to certain encrypted signals — a feature Solenne officially denies building in.
One chip on every Solenne Datalink bracelet is factory-reserved and cannot be written by the owner; what Solenne stores there is the subject of considerable Spire paranoia.

physical_description.visual_profile: A substantial, statement-making cuff bracelet that commands wrist presence. The wide band creates an almost architectural quality, catching light with prismatic shifts. Simultaneously luxurious and functional—reads as high-tier corpo accessory meeting utilitarian tech integration. The continuous opal inlay gives it an almost hypnotic quality that draws the eye.
physical_description.fit: Snug cuff fit, sits firmly on the wrist without movement. The fold-over clasp ensures secure closure. Width spans approximately 1.5-2 inches across the wrist, substantial but not bulky. Ergonomically designed for all-day wear despite tech integration.
physical_description.primary_material: 22-carat gold-analog plating over titanium substrate. Lab-grown black opal continuous inlay band. White gold-analog fold-over clasp. Passive data-chip array embedded in titanium backing.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, polished metal surfaces with a satin finish on the gold-analog plating. The opal surface is glassy and reflective, slightly cooler to touch than the metal. Titanium backing feels lightweight but substantial. Clasp has subtle texture from the Solenne Spire mark stamp.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: warm champagne gold-analog with deep matte black opal centerline. Secondary: crisp white gold-analog clasp. The opal shifts dynamically—deep violet in cool light, burnished copper-green in warm light, creating a living color palette.
physical_description.closures: Japanese-style fold-over clasp in white gold-analog, pressure-fit with subtle magnetic reinforcement for security. No visible locks or complications—elegant minimalism.
distinctive_features: Continuous band of lab-grown black opal with dynamic light-shift properties
Twelve embedded passive data-chips along inner face, invisible when worn
Solenne Spire atelier mark stamped into clasp—recognizable hallmark of Tier 1 luxury craftsmanship
Titanium substrate for durability and lightweight feel despite precious metal plating
Architectural cuff proportions that reference both jewelry tradition and tech-forward design
Encrypted data architecture—functions as secure wallet and identity suite
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 luxury. Price point alone signals corpo elite. Solenne Atelier positioning as exclusive atelier brand, not mass-market. Gold-analog plating and lab-grown opal indicate refined taste and access to premium materials.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is established corpo hierarchy, likely financial services or biotech sector. Signals trustworthiness and secure access—the bracelet is a literal credential suite. Wearing this announces you have encrypted secrets worth protecting and the wealth to afford them. Also signals refined aesthetic taste; this is jewelry first, tech second. Not military, not street, not sub-grade. Pure corpo luxury.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly broken-in. Solenne pieces are heirloom-grade; owners maintain them meticulously. Opal may show dust or residue in certain light angles that requires gentle cleaning. Gold-analog plating retains shine through passive care. Clasp develops subtle patina over years of use but remains functional.
